descriptions.conditions: A banking-company amalgamation under section 44A requires a draft scheme placed separately before each company's shareholders, approval by a majority in number representing two-thirds in value of shareholders present personally or by proxy, and submission of the approved scheme to the Reserve Bank for sanction.
descriptions.effect: If the Reserve Bank sanctions the scheme in writing, it binds the banking companies and shareholders; the amalgamated company's property and liabilities transfer to the acquiring banking company by virtue of the sanction order, subject to the sanctioned scheme. The Reserve Bank may separately direct dissolution.
descriptions.scope_and_exceptions: This unit governs the section 44A procedure for amalgamation of banking companies, including meeting notice, dissenting-shareholder valuation rights, sanction, vesting, dissolution and evidentiary consequences. It does not itself establish immunity from lease, tenancy or rent restrictions. Central Government amalgamation power identified in subsection (7) is preserved, subject to consultation with the Reserve Bank.

descriptions.conditions: Where the Reserve Bank considers there is good reason, it may seek a Central Government moratorium for a banking company. During a moratorium or at any other time, the Reserve Bank may prepare a reconstruction or amalgamation scheme when satisfied that this is necessary in the public interest, depositors' interests, proper management, or the interests of the banking system as a whole.
descriptions.effect: After the draft consultation process, the Central Government may sanction the scheme with or without modifications. From the operative date, the sanctioned scheme binds specified companies, members, depositors, creditors, employees and other persons with relevant rights or liabilities; property, assets and liabilities transfer to the transferee bank only to the extent provided in the scheme.
descriptions.scope_and_exceptions: Section 45 supplies the RBI/Central Government moratorium, reconstruction and amalgamation regime and permits scheme provisions concerning assets, liabilities, proceedings, creditor and member interests, employees and consequential matters. Section 45 and schemes under it override contrary laws, agreements, awards or instruments. Any modification or exemption concerning law governing acquired business is recommendation-based and limited to seven years. The text does not itself identify lease or rent-control consequences.
